cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 2nd District since 2013. Attorney who was a senior attorney at the Natural Resources Defense Council and served 12 years on the Marin Municipal Water District board. Served in the California Assembly 2006-2012. Ranking Member of House Natural Resources.

controversies.text: Missed 17 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (2.5%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 3, 2025-06-09 to 2025-06-09.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements include the California Democratic Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, IUOE Local 3, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and California Young Democrats.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance or action by Huffman on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buying, or school vouchers and charters. We found nothing on state-level police pay and pensions, gun laws or H-1B. We also found no deed or statement on growth limits or land protection that clearly maps to slowing development, and no pledge to refuse donor money. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through the 118th Congress key votes. His birth city is documented, but his childhood is only partly documented: we know he graduated high school in Independence, Missouri. We could not confirm the exact year he first came to California.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Robin Littau
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 2nd Congressional District. U.S. Coast Guard veteran (1997-2001, machinery technician). Elected member of the Enterprise Elementary School District board in Redding (2024-26). Owns Rockin Robin's Cleaning Service and Joyful Living Magazine.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from Reform California, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, April's Common Sense Cali Voters and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide. In her own survey she also names the Shasta County and Sonoma Republican Central Committees.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or actions by Robin Littau on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor purchases of California land, H-1B visas, guns, abortion or school choice. Her campaign site names broad themes such as immigration reform, cutting regulation and parental rights, without specifics we could match to these topics. We found no record of her votes or actions on the Enterprise Elementary School District board. Her birth city is not given. Her claims about military service, the school board seat and the 2025 Mary Beth Weiss Award come from her own site and survey and were not checked against independent records. We found no controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 55: She says she was born and raised in South Dakota and has lived in California for 28 years, since her Coast Guard posting in Alameda, which makes her an adult arrival more than 25 years ago.

score.why: Raised $0, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Currently an elected school board member (Enterprise Elementary School District, 2024-26). U.S. Coast Guard diesel mechanic 1997-2001. Sole proprietor of a cleaning company for about 10 years and new owner of a local magazine. She has no legislative, legal or executive governing record beyond the school board.
qual.why: Local elected office and small-business management fall in the middle band. Her record is otherwise thin for federal lawmaking, oversight and budgeting, so the score sits at the lower end of that band.
